docs.title: Introduction - JawaScript
docs.text:
A script built in Javanese Language, a language that is easy to use and implement and has the same structure as JavaScript because it is only a translation.

Info

This project was inspired by RioChndr/jaksel-language, thanks for inspiring me! and i'm not focusing on the top priority of this project, but if you want to try developing or updating on my repo please do, if there are any problems please report them, this is also just entertainment material.

docs.title: How does this happen
docs.text: Where in this script there is one file to define all the syntax from Javanese to javascript which is really common javascript, everything is done without any library just enough to overwrite and translate it into javascript.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
You can simply install it into the global module on npm or yarn, you are free to use what you want but give this script to global.

npm i -g jawascript@https://github.com/ernestoyoofi/jawascript

Then to run the script use a command like this

jawaskrip <filename>.jawa
# or use
jawaskrip <filename>.jw

For you to try to build this jawascript into javascript use the --dir flag or arg and then forward the folder you want to build to

jawaskrip --dir ./myproject

docs.title: Syntax Class
docs.text:
In general, you can also use it in javascript, but here you can also use it like this

taterapan person {
  kontruksi() {
    this.name = "Person"
  }
  harisekarang() {
    return anyar Wektu()
  }
}

It will automatically become

class person {
  constructor() {
    this.name = "Person"
  }
  harisekarang() {
    return new Date()
  }
}

docs.title: Syntax Data Type
docs.text:
This section still has a lot of improvements, although I don't know when it will be fixed.

In general, you can still use native / common from javascript, but you can also replace it with something like this

  • "wilangan": "number"
  • "kata": "string"
  • oraono: "undefined"
  • "obyek": "object"
  • opoTatanan: Array.isArray Functionable
  • opoWilangan: !isNaN Functionable

For the example :

typeof 4 == "wilangan" // Number / Numeric
typeof 'it me!' == "kata" // String
typeof undefined == oraono // Undefined
typeof {} == 'obyek' // Object
typeof [{}] == 'obyek' // ObjectArray
opoTatanan([]) // will return the result value `true`
opoTatanan({}) // will return the result value `false`
opoWilangan('4') // will return the result value `true`
opoWilangan('8eelf') // will return the result value `false`

docs.title: Syntax Error
docs.text:
If you want to take the problem on asyncronus or not so that the script does not close immediately you can use like this

nyobake {
  mbalangi perkoroAnyar("Oops!")
} njupuk(e) {
  infoPerkoro(a. stack)
} akire {
  catetan("Rampung!")
}

Then the above script becomes like this

try {
  throw new Error("Oops!")
} catch(e) {
  console.error(a.stack)
} finally {
  console.log("Rampung!")
}

docs.title: Syntax Function
docs.text:
Here I use the word fungsi because I don't have any options for some Javanese words for Function.

Example:

fungsi tambah(a, b) {
  catetan("Menambahkan ", a, " dan ", b)
  return a + b
}

docs.title: Syntax Log & Debugging
docs.text:
Quite simple, where you usually use the console to view some of the data, here you can also but only provide 2, namely :

  • infoPerkoro : console.error
  • catetan : console.log

infoPerkoro("Error!")
// become as
console.error("Error!")
And

catetan("Yeaa!")
// become as
console.log("Yeaa!")

docs.title: Syntax Looping
docs.text:
There is only one looping system at the moment, it is not possible to implement all of them because it is difficult.

Here if you want to use for as looping data you can replace it with ubengi which means “to loop”.

For example:

ubengi(let a of [1,2,3]) {
  catetan(a)
}
// become as
for(let a of [1,2,3]) {
  console.log(a)
}

docs.title: Syntax Operation
docs.text:
Some suitable keywords to say in place of less than, more than and not the same, here simply write as listed here :

  • luwihSeko : more than → >
  • luwihSitik : less than → <
  • oraSepadan : not the same → !==

And for some operations like if else if and else are replaced like this:

  • naliko : if
  • liyane : else
  • ukoro : else if

For example see below

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
naliko(a luwihSeko b) {
  catetan("luwih seko")
} ukoro(a luwihSitik c) {
  catetan("luwih sitik")
  naliko(c luwihSeko d) {
    infoPerkoro("ana masalah")
  }
} liyane {
  catetan("-")
}

docs.title: luwihSeko / More than
docs.text:
naliko(a luwihSeko b) {
  catetan("luwih seko")
}

and automatically in javascript like this

if(a > b) {
  console.log("luwih seko")
}

docs.title: luwihSitik / Less than
docs.text:
naliko(a luwihSitik b) {
  catetan("luwih sitik")
}

and automatically in javascript like this

if(a < b) {
  console.log("luwih sitik")
}

docs.title: oraSepadan / Not the same
docs.text:
naliko(a oraSepadan b) {
  catetan("ora podo")
}

and automatically in javascript like this

if(a !== b) {
  console.log("ora podo")
}

docs.title: Syntax True & False
docs.text:
Bug

This section still has a lot of improvements, although I don't know when it will be fixed.

You can use several types, here are two, just use one of them :

  • iyo mean true
  • nggih mean true
  • ora mean false
  • mboten mean false

For the example :

konstan isData iku iyo
// become as
const isData = true

docs.title: Syntax Variable
docs.text:
In general, you can use variables in javascript like this

const a = "Kulo"
var b = "Sampean"
let c = 5
let d;

But you can also use it here like this

konstan data = "Kulo"
konstan dataOne iku "Kulo"
variable dataTelu = "Sampean"
variable dataPapat iku "Sampean"
benkedata dataLima = 5
benkedata dataEnem;
